title: Git Essentials for Pipeline Work
intro: Every pipeline is triggered by git, and every pipeline investigation starts with 'what exactly changed?'. These are the commands that answer it.

steps.prompt: See what's changed in your working directory and what's staged.
steps.fake_output:
On branch feature/cart
Changes to be committed:
	modified:   src/cart.js
Changes not staged for commit:
	modified:   .github/workflows/ci.yml
Untracked files:
	.env
steps.explanation: One file staged, one modified but unstaged, and an untracked .env.
steps.why: Run this before every commit. That untracked .env almost certainly contains secrets — seeing it here is your chance to add it to .gitignore instead of committing it with a careless 'git add .'.

steps.prompt: See the exact line changes in the unstaged workflow file.
steps.fake_output:
-        run: npm test
+        run: npm test -- --passWithNoTests
steps.explanation: Someone changed the test step to pass even when no tests are found.
steps.why: That's the kind of quiet change that makes a pipeline 'green' while testing nothing. Reviewing diffs to CI config deserves extra scrutiny for exactly this reason. Use 'git diff --staged' to see what's already staged.

steps.prompt: Show the last 10 commits as one line each.
steps.fake_output:
e4f5a6b (HEAD -> feature/cart) add discount codes
c3d4e5f fix cart total rounding
a1b2c3d (origin/main, main) release v2.3.0
steps.explanation: Two commits on the feature branch on top of main.
steps.why: The short hashes here are what pipelines report ('build failed on c3d4e5f'), and what you pass to revert, cherry-pick, and checkout. --graph adds a branch diagram, useful for understanding merges.

steps.prompt: Download the latest changes from the remote without modifying your working branch.
steps.explanation: origin/main moved forward; your local branches are untouched.
steps.why: 'git pull' = fetch + merge in one step, which can surprise you with a merge you didn't intend. Fetching first lets you inspect incoming changes (git log main..origin/main) before integrating them.

steps.prompt: You need to switch branches urgently to fix a bug, but you have uncommitted work. Set it aside temporarily.
steps.fake_output: Saved working directory and index state WIP on feature/cart: e4f5a6b add discount codes
steps.explanation: Your changes are saved on a stack; the working directory is now clean.
steps.why: Committing half-finished work just to switch branches pollutes history. Stash is the clean temporary shelf. Add -u to include untracked files.

steps.prompt: The urgent fix is done. Bring your stashed work back.
steps.fake_output:
On branch feature/cart
Changes not staged for commit:
	modified:   .github/workflows/ci.yml
Dropped refs/stash@{0}
steps.explanation: Changes restored and removed from the stash stack.
steps.why: 'pop' applies and deletes; 'apply' applies but keeps a copy in the stash. If pop hits a conflict, the stash is kept so you don't lose anything.
